summary: Google Research's time-series forecasting model TimesFM-3 (330.7M parameters in F32) was measured for fit and speed only, since no bench here rates a forecaster: its own Python package (timesfm 3.0.2) on the PyTorch of the pinned vLLM image, with vLLM itself not imported, ran a fixed grid of synthetic series first on one card, then on 8 vCPU with no card. It loaded in about 2 s, 1,262 MiB of the card allocated by torch. On the card one series with a 512-point context and a 64-point horizon took 143 ms (median), 32 series with a 2,048-point context and a 128-point horizon 443 ms, about 72 series a second, and batches of up to 256 series fit at its full 15,360-point context, where 512 ran out of memory. On the CPU alone the same 32-series call took about 3.0 s (10.7 series a second) and one series at the full context about 1.0 s. No energy figure is given. The model's licence allows non-commercial use and internal benchmarking and forbids distributing it: its figures are published here, no copy of the model is.
title: TimesFM-3: fit and speed on one RTX 3090 and on the CPU alone
